g.text: Does a less diverse window go with more repetition?
Two measurements for each word, using its recorded position on the page.
Earlier words above and just to the left.
Slide a 100-word window across the same word.
Outlined otedy: target. Other labeled boxes: its sources.
8 lines up, 45° half-angle; 3 word widths left.
At most 100 sources; nearer words count more.
More varied, more evenly used pairs → higher diversity.
Each bar is 100 words. Colored squares are otedy.
Three of the 100 containing windows are shown.
Compare words with less and more diverse source windows
Within each bifolium, compare the lowest and highest fifths of source diversity.
Do this separately for small, medium and large source pools, then average.
Positive contrast: more repetition when the nearby components are less diverse.
